newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai commission approves new draft constitution.
newsitem.headline: Thai commission approves new draft constitution.

text.p: Thailand's Constitution Drafting Assembly (CDA) on Friday gave final approval to a controversial new draft constitution for the country.

Delegates in the 99-member CDA, who earlier hailed the draft as a historical charter ushering in political reforms against money politics and curbing traditional military interference in government, voted 92-0 for the draft. There were three abstentions and four CDA members were absent during the vote.

"As chairman of CDA, I would like to express my appreciation to CDA members and all parties concerned who share this period of pride in achieving a crucial service for the country," former prime minister Anand Panyarachun said after the vote.
The new constitution contains hotly debated clauses aimed at curbing military influence in politics, and provisions for checks and balances against money politics and vote buying.
The approved draft will be debated by a joint session of Thailand's 393-member House of Representatives and 262-member Senate early next month.
Thai elder statesman Praves Vasi and political activists urged politicians to vote for the new constitution to show their support for political reforms.
But not everyone backed the new draft constitution.
"I will not vote for a constitution that has been drafted by a group of people influenced by dictatorial opinions," said deputy prime minister Samak Sundaravej.

Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh, who had earlier been reluctant to back the constitution, on Friday vowed to push for its final passage and reiterated his promise to call a new general election within two years.

"For those fearing the nation will face unrest if the draft constitution fails to sail through parliament, please don't worry. This government will push for its passage. I will keep my words to step down within two years," Chavalit said.
Chavalit had vowed during his election campaign last year that he would push for constitutional reforms.

But Sanoh Thienthong, interior minister and secretary general of Chavalit's New Aspiration Party (NAP), warned supporters of the new constitution that it would result in chaos and social confrontation if adopted.
Senators appointed from the armed forces said they would vote for the constitution.

"Even though some generals are not happy with the draft, we will vote for the bill first and later propose amendments. Otherwise we may be blamed for instigating unrest in the country," a senior army officer told Reuters.
